neighbor_ip.description: The IP address of the external BGP peer.

neighbor_port.description: The port number for the external BGP peer. Default is 179.

address.description: The static IP address of the endpoint, required for static endpoints.

connection_type_ref.description: This represents a connection type used in endpoints, which defines the connectivity group, mode, and link type for VPN connections.

dynamic.description: Indicates whether the endpoint is dynamic (true) or static (false).

enabled.description: Indicates whether the endpoint is enabled (true) or disabled (false).

etag.description: The ETag of the element, used for versioning. This field is not required.

force_nat_t.description: Indicates whether the endpoint forces NAT Traversal (NAT_T) for VPN connections.

id.description: this attribute is the identifier of terraform resource

ike_phase1_id_type.description: The type of Phase-1 ID used for the endpoint, represented as a single digit. '0' for DNS_NAME, '1' for EMAIL, '2' for DISTINGUISHED_NAME, and '3' for IP_ADDRESS.

ike_phase1_id_value.description: The value of the Phase-1 ID for the endpoint, which must match the specified Phase-1 ID type.

key.description: The unique identifier for the element. This field is required for updates but not for creation.

locked.description: Indicates if the element is locked. This field is not required.

nat_t.description: Indicates whether the endpoint supports NAT Traversal (NAT_T) for VPN connections.

read_only.description: Indicates if the element is read-only. This field is not required.

system.description: Indicates if the element is a System element. This field is not required.

system_key.description: The system key of the System element. This field is not required.

trashed.description: Indicates if the element is trashed. This field is not required.

udp_encapsulation.description: Indicates whether the endpoint supports UDP encapsulation for VPN tunnels.

block.description: This represents an external endpoint for VPN connections, supporting both tunnel and portal types. It includes properties such as physical interface and deducted name.

admin_domain.description: This represents a Domain. Domains are administrative boundaries that allow you to separate the configuration details and other information in the system for the purpose of limiting administrator access.

comment.description: An optional comment for the element. This field is not required.

etag.description: The ETag of the element, used for versioning. This field is not required.

gateway_profile.description: Gateway Profiles describe the capabilities of a Gateway, i.e. supported cipher, hash, etc. Gateway Profiles of Internal Gateways are read-only and computed from Firewall version and FIPS mode. Gateway Profiles of External Gateways are user-defined.

id.description: this attribute is the identifier of terraform resource

key.description: The unique identifier for the element. This field is required for updates but not for creation.

locked.description: Indicates if the element is locked. This field is not required.

read_only.description: Indicates if the element is read-only. This field is not required.

system.description: Indicates if the element is a System element. This field is not required.

system_key.description: The system key of the System element. This field is not required.

trashed.description: Indicates if the element is trashed. This field is not required.

trust_all_cas.description: Indicates whether the External Gateway trusts all VPN Certificate Authorities. If true, it does not require specific trusted CAs.

trusted_certificate_authorities.description: URI of the trusted VPN Certificate Authority.

block.description: This represents an External Gateway, which is used for establishing VPN connections with external networks. It includes gateway profile, trust settings for VPN certificate authorities, and lists of end-points and sites.

active_server_certificate_probing.description: Flag for enabling/disabling TLS probe connections.

active_wait_time.description: The Active Wait Time. 'short' Short, 'medium' Medium, 'long' Long.

admin_auth_method.description: This represents an external authentication method, which can be used for user authentication in the system. It supports various types of authentication methods such as User Password, IAS, IPSec, Pre-Shared Key, RADIUS, TACACS+, and LDAP.

admin_domain.description: This represents a Domain. Domains are administrative boundaries that allow you to separate the configuration details and other information in the system for the purpose of limiting administrator access.

allow_email_upn_lookup.description: Indicates whether email UPN lookup is allowed. If true, the system allows lookup from known User Domain matching to client certificate email domain or UPN suffix.

allow_long_userid_lookup.description: Indicates whether long UserID lookup is allowed. If true, the system allows username lookup using Long UserID attribute.

allow_root_login.description: Indicates whether root login is allowed for administrator authentication. Options include 'allow' for allowing root login, 'disable_pwd_ssh' for disabling root password login through SSH, and 'disable' for disabling all root password logins, including console access.

antispoofing_node_ref.description: This represents an Antispoofing Node in the Security Management Client, which is used to protect against malicious packages with altered IP header information.

auto_reboot_timeout.description: The length of time after which an error situation is considered non-recoverable and the engine automatically reboots. The default value is 10 seconds.

client_cert_identity_field.description: The Client Certificate Identity Field that defines how the client certificate identity is determined.

cluster_mode.description: Defines the clustering mode of the engine. Options are 'balancing' for simultaneous online nodes or 'standby' for one node online at a time.

comment.description: An optional comment for the element. This field is not required.

connection_limit.description: Sets a limit for connections from a single source and/or destination IP address. When the set number of connections is reached, the next connection attempts are blocked by the engine until a previously open connection is closed.

contact_timeout.description: Used when opening any kind of communication between the Management Server and the engines. A consistently slow network connection may require increasing this value. The default value is 60 seconds.

control_plane_mode.description: The control plane mode of the Master Engine, which determines the allocation of CPU resources for control plane operations. Options include 'not_reserved' for no dedicated CPU allocation, 'one_cpu' for 1 CPU allocated, 'two_cpus' for 2 CPUs allocated, 'three_cpus' for 3 CPUs allocated, and 'four_cpus' for 4 CPUs allocated.

custom_properties_profile.description: URI of the custom properties profile.

default_nat.description: Indicates whether the Default NAT Address is used for Traffic from Internal Networks. It can be set to 'true', 'false', or 'automatic'.

default_user_domain.description: This represents a User Domain, which is used to define the authentication domain for users. It can be either an authentication domain or the internal domain.

destination_server_certificate_cache_tim.description: The timeout value for certificate entries in the cache in minutes.

disable_ahm.description: Indicates whether Application Health Monitoring (AHM) is disabled. If true, AHM is not performed for the Firewall Cluster.

discard_quic_if_cant_inspect.description: Indicates whether QUIC traffic should be discarded when inspection is not possible.

dns_relay_profile_ref.description: This represents a DNS Relay profile element, which contains settings for hostname mappings, domain-specific DNS servers, fixed domain answers, and DNS answer translations.

dos_protection.description: The DOS Protection Mode that defines the level of protection against Denial of Service attacks. It can be set to 'always_off', 'default_off', or 'default_on'.

enable_saml_for_application_access.description: Indicates whether the SAML authentication method is enabled for Application Access Portal. If true, SAML authentication is used for Application Access Portal.

enable_saml_for_bba.description: Indicates whether the SAML authentication method is enabled for user authentication (BBA). If true, SAML authentication is used for browser-based authentication.

engine_version.description: The version of the engine that this cluster is running.

etag.description: The ETag of the element, used for versioning. This field is not required.

excluded_interface.description: The ID of the interface that is excluded from IP counting. By default, not defined.

failover_time.description: The clustering heartbeat failover time in milliseconds. This defines the time after which a node is considered failed if no heartbeat is received.

filter_mode.description: Defines how traffic is balanced between the nodes. Options are 'static' for fixed packet ownership or 'dynamic' for load balancing.

fuid_network_filter.description: The network filtering address ranges for the engine. It is used by the firewall to restrict the range of events to be received from the FUID server.

gateway_settings_ref.description: This represents various gateway and VPN parameters to be set at Firewall level. These settings are used for the negotiation of VPN connections.

geolocation_ref.description: This represents the definition of a geolocation. A Geolocation object keeps a list of Network Elements belonging to the same geolocation.

half_open_connections.description: The number of Half Open Connections allowed. If not specified, it defaults to 125.

id.description: this attribute is the identifier of terraform resource

include_interfaces_for_control_plane.description: Indicates whether interfaces used for management and log connections are included in the control plane. If true, these interfaces are included in the control plane operations.

inspection_cpu_balancing_mode.description: The Inspection CPU Balancing Mode. 'default' Default value, 'round_robin' Round Robin, 'numa' NUMA local Round Robin.

integrated_uis_ref.description: This represents an Integrated User Identification Service, which is used to identify users based on their network activity. It allows for integration with authentication domains and provides configuration options for initial query time, polling interval, and ignore values.

is_cert_auto_renewal.description: Indicates whether automated certificate renewal is enabled for this cluster.

is_fips_compatible_operating_mode.description: Indicates whether the FIPS mode is enabled. FIPS standard specifies the security requirements that will be satisfied by a cryptographic module utilized within a security system protecting sensitive but unclassified information.

is_fips_disable_engine_sginfo.description: Indicates whether the creation of sginfo for engines in FIPS mode is disabled.

is_fips_disable_engine_upgrades.description: Indicates whether the ability to remotely upgrade engines in FIPS mode is disabled.

is_icap_dlp_enabled.description: Indicates whether ICAP DLP (Data Loss Prevention) is enabled.

is_loopback_tunnel_ip_address_enforced.description: Indicates whether the Loopback Tunnel IP is enforced. If true, the Loopback Tunnel IP is used instead of the default outgoing IP if no IP Address is provided on Tunnel Interfaces.

is_snort_enabled.description: Indicates whether Snort intrusion detection and prevention is enabled for the firewall cluster.

is_snort_file_defined.description: Indicates whether a Snort configuration file is defined for the firewall cluster.

is_virtual_defrag.description: Defines whether virtual defragmentation is enabled, which allows the engine to handle fragmented packets during inspection.

key.description: The unique identifier for the element. This field is required for updates but not for creation.

known_host_lists_ref.description: URI of the Known Host List.

lbfilter_useports.description: Indicates whether the Load Balancing Filter uses ports. If true, the filter will consider port numbers in its operations.

link_usage_profile_ref.description: This represents a Link Usage Profile, which is used to manage link usage settings in a multi-link environment. It includes configurations for link balancing, packet duplication, and forward erasure correction.

lldp_profile_ref.description: This represents a LLDP Profile, which is used to configure the LLDP (Link Layer Discovery Protocol) settings for devices.

location_ref.description: This represents the definition of a Location, which keeps a list of Network Elements belonging to the same location.

locked.description: Indicates if the element is locked. This field is not required.

log_server_ref.description: This represents a Log Server, which is a component of the Management Center responsible for storing and managing log (and alert) data, and analyzing and correlating events detected by multiple NGFW Engines.

log_spooling_policy.description: The Log Spooling Policy that defines what happens when the engine's log spool becomes full. It can be set to 'stop' (Stop Traffic) or 'discard' (Discard Log).

message_period.description: The clustering heartbeat message period in milliseconds. This defines how often the cluster nodes send heartbeat messages to each other.

multicast_routing_mode.description: The Multicast Routing Mode that defines how multicast traffic is handled. 'none' disables the multicast routing. 'static' enables the Static multicast routing. 'igmp_proxy' enables the IGMP Proxy multicast routing. 'pim_ipv4' enables the PIM multicast routing.

nondecrypted_ca_certificate_ref.description: URI of the non-decrypted CA certificates.

nondecrypted_tls_server_credentials_ref.description: URI of the non-decrypted TLS server credentials.

passive_discard_mode.description: Indicates whether the Passive Discard Mode is enabled. If true, it does not stop matching connections but creates a special log entry Terminate (passive) for testing purposes.

quic_enabled.description: Indicates whether QUIC ports are enabled for Web Traffic. If true, QUIC protocol is allowed for web traffic.

read_only.description: Indicates if the element is read-only. This field is not required.

reporting_email_addresses.description: The contact email address for reporting per sender.

rollback_timeout.description: The time the engine waits for a management connection before it rolls back to the previously installed policy when the Policy Handshake option is active. The default value is 60 seconds.

routing_node_ref.description: This represents a Routing Node in the Security Management Client, which is used to configure routing for network traffic on firewalls.

saml_application_access_clock_skew.description: The clock skew for SAML Application Access authentication in seconds. It defines the allowed time difference between the SAML assertion and the system time.

saml_bba_clock_skew.description: The clock skew for SAML BBA authentication in seconds. It defines the allowed time difference between the SAML assertion and the system time.

send_reset_for_out_of_state_tcp_packets.description: The engine refuses TCP connections if the TCP connection does not start with a SYN packet, even if the TCP connection matches an Access rule with the Allow action.

server_credential.description: URI of the TLS Server Credentials.

sidewinder_logging_profile_ref.description: This represents a Sidewinder Logging Profile, which contains settings for logging in Sidewinder.

sidewinder_proxy_enabled.description: Indicates whether the Sidewinder Proxy is enabled. If true, the Sidewinder Proxy is used for enhanced security and logging.

slow_request_block_list_timeout.description: The DOS Protection Slow Request Block List timeout in seconds. It defines how long a slow request is blocked before it can be retried.

slow_request_sensitivity.description: The DOS Protection Slow Request Sensitivity that defines the sensitivity level for slow requests. It can be set to 'off', 'low', 'medium', or 'high'.

snmp_agent_ref.description: This represents an SNMP Agent. It contains the configuration details for SNMP (Simple Network Management Protocol) on an engine, including SNMP version, users, monitoring settings, and trap destinations.

snmp_location.description: The location for the current SNMP client.

ssh_passwordless_login.description: Indicates whether SSH passwordless logins are allowed for administrator authentication. Options include 'allow' for allowing passwordless logins and 'deny' for denying them.

strict_tcp_mode.description: Indicates whether Strict TCP mode is enabled. When enabled, it provides enhanced protection against TCP evasion attempts by controlling the progress of a TCP connection and enforcing the order of packets.

syn_flood_sensitivity.description: The DOS Protection Syn Flood Sensitivity that defines the sensitivity level for SYN flood attacks. It can be set to 'off', 'low', 'medium', or 'high'.

syn_max_bursts.description: The SYN Burst Size value (>= 1). The number of allowed SYNs before the engine starts limiting the SYN rate.

syn_mode.description: The SYN Rate Limits Mode. 'off' SYN Rate Limits are disabled. This is the default setting. 'auto' The engine automatically calculates the number of Allowed SYNs per Second and the Burst Size for the interface based on the engine's capacity and memory size. 'custom' Enter the desired values for Allowed SYNs per Second and Burst Size. We recommend that the Burst Size be at least one tenth of the Allowed SYNs per Second value. If the Burst Size is too small, SYN Rate Limits do not work.

syn_per_second.description: The Allowed SYNs per Second value (>= 1). The number of allowed SYN packets per second.

system.description: Indicates if the element is a System element. This field is not required.

system_key.description: The system key of the System element. This field is not required.

tcp_reset_sensitivity.description: The DOS TCP Reset Sensitivity that defines the sensitivity level for TCP reset attacks. It can be set to 'off', 'low', 'medium', or 'high'.

timezone.description: The timezone setting for the firewall, which determines the local time zone used by the system.

tls_crl_checks.description: Indicates whether the engine performs CRL checks for TLS certificates.

tls_cryptography_suite_set_ref.description: This represents a TLS Cryptography Suite Set Element, which contains a set of cryptographic suites used in SSL VPN configurations.

tls_deny_decrypting.description: Indicates whether the engine denies decrypting TLS traffic.

tools_profile_ref.description: This represents a Tools Profile. Tools Profiles add commands to the right-click menus of elements, allowing dynamic information inclusion from the element definition. Only one Tools Profile can be selected for each element, but each can include several commands. Commands are launched on the workstation running the Management Client and are operating-system-specific.

tracking_mode.description: The Connection Tracking Mode. 'normal' When selected, the engine drops ICMP error messages related to connections that are not currently active in connection tracking. A valid, complete TCP handshake is required for TCP traffic. The engine checks the traffic direction and the port parameters of UDP traffic. 'strict' When selected, the engine does not permit TCP traffic to pass through before a complete, valid TCP handshake is performed. 'loose' When selected, the engine allows some connection patterns and address translation operations that are not allowed in the Normal mode. Note! You can override this general setting and configure connection tracking for TCP, UDP, and ICMP traffic in Access rules.

trashed.description: Indicates if the element is trashed. This field is not required.

user_id_service_ref.description: This represents a User ID Service element, which is used to manage user identification services. It includes attributes for port, IP addresses, monitored user domains, cache expiration, connect timeout, TLS profile, and TLS identity.

activate_failover.description: The time in seconds to activate failover after the threshold is reached.

dpd_initial_values.description: The initial values for DPD (Dead Peer Detection) settings, which can be used to configure the initial state of the Multi-Link.

failover_initial_values.description: The initial values for failover settings, which can be used to configure the initial state of the Multi-Link.

failover_prop_high.description: The failover property high, which is a percentage value that indicates the threshold for high failover conditions.

failover_threshold.description: The failover threshold, which determines the number of failed probes before a failover is triggered.

in_traffic_initial_values.description: The initial values for in-traffic settings, which can be used to configure the initial state of the Multi-Link.

latency_initial_values.description: The initial values for latency settings, which can be used to configure the initial state of the Multi-Link.

multilink_extra_options.description: Additional options for Multi-Link settings, which can be used to configure extra parameters for the Multi-Link.

pdr_initial_values.description: The initial values for PDR (Packet Delivery Ratio) settings, which can be used to configure the initial state of the Multi-Link.

probe_threshold.description: The probe threshold, which is a percentage value that indicates the threshold for probing the links.

remoteload_initial_values.description: The initial values for remote load settings, which can be used to configure the initial state of the Multi-Link.

throughput_initial_values.description: The initial values for throughput settings, which can be used to configure the initial state of the Multi-Link.

block.description: This represents the advanced Multi-Link settings for the engine, which includes failover thresholds, probe thresholds, and initial values for various parameters.

alias_ref.description: This represents a network element, which is a component that has an IP address and can be part of a network. It includes a location reference.

cluster_ref.description: This represents a group of devices, or nodes, that share a given work load. You can cluster Firewalls, IPS engines, and Layer 2 Firewalls to share the load and provide redundancy, allowing, for example, scheduled maintenance that takes one node out of service without interrupting services to the users.

resolved_value.description: The resolved values for the Alias, which are the actual values used in the policies.

translated_element.description: URI of the Network Element used as translated element.

antivirus_enabled.description: Indicates whether the antivirus feature is enabled on the firewall element.

antivirus_http_proxy_enabled.description: Indicates whether the HTTP Proxy is enabled for antivirus updates. By default, it is not enabled.

antivirus_proxy_password.description: The HTTP Proxy password used for authentication when accessing the antivirus update server.

antivirus_proxy_port.description: The HTTP Proxy port used for antivirus updates.

antivirus_proxy_user.description: The HTTP Proxy username used for authentication when accessing the antivirus update server.

antivirus_update.description: The frequency at which the antivirus updates are performed.

antivirus_update_day.description: The day of the week when antivirus updates are performed, represented as a two-letter abbreviation.

antivirus_update_time.description: The time of the day the Antivirus updates are performed, given as a long value in a 24-hour format.

virus_alert.description: This represents an abstract Alert, which is used to display messages when certain conditions are met.

virus_log_level.description: The log level for antivirus events, which determines how antivirus-related logs are handled.

virus_mirror.description: The URL of the antivirus signature mirrors used for updating malware signatures.

block.description: This represents the settings for the antivirus feature on a firewall element, including antivirus enablement, log levels, update frequencies, and proxy settings.

alert_ref.description: This represents an abstract Alert, which is used to display messages when certain conditions are met.

allow_auth_traffic.description: Indicates whether authentication traffic is allowed for this Automatic Rules Settings.

allow_connections_to_dns_resolvers.description: Indicates whether connections to DNS resolvers are allowed for this Automatic Rules Settings.

allow_connections_to_remote_dhcp_server.description: Indicates whether connections to a remote DHCP server are allowed for this Automatic Rules Settings.

allow_icmp_traffic_for_route_probing.description: Indicates whether ICMP traffic is allowed for route probing in this Automatic Rules Settings.

allow_listening_interfaces_to_dns_relay_.description: Indicates whether listening interfaces are allowed to relay DNS traffic for this Automatic Rules Settings.

allow_no_nat.description: Indicates whether NAT is allowed to be bypassed for this Automatic Rules Settings.

log_level.description: The log level for the Automatic Rules Settings, which defines the verbosity of logging.

qos_class_ref.description: This represents a QoS Class, which is an element that links a rule in a QoS Policy to one or more Firewall Actions. The traffic allowed in the access rule is assigned the QoS Class defined for the rule, and the QoS class is used as the matching criteria for applying QoS Policy rules.

vpn_ref.description: This represents a Policy Based Virtual Private Network (VPN), which is used to establish secure connections over unsecured networks. It includes various configurations such as NAT rules, mobile VPN topology modes, and associated profiles.

block.description: This represents the Automatic Rules Settings for the Engine Cluster, including VPN, QoS Class, Alert, and various traffic control settings.

crl_distribution_point_list.description: A list of URLs representing the distribution points to use for CRL (Certificate Revocation List) cache on the engine.

http_proxy_ref.description: This represents an HTTP Proxy, which is used to route HTTP traffic through a proxy server. It includes attributes for IP address, port, username, and password.

ocsp_crl_timeout.description: The timeout in seconds for OCSP and CRL lookups. This setting determines how long the engine will wait for a response before timing out.

block.description: This defines settings for certificate validation on the engine, including OCSP and CRL lookups, timeout settings, and optional HTTP proxy configuration.

protocol.description: The protocol for which the idle timeout is defined. Default values are 'udp', 'tcp', 'icmp', and 'other'.

timeout.description: The timeout duration in seconds for idle connections.

address.description: The IP address associated with the single Physical Interface, VLAN Interface, Modem Interface, ADSL Interface, or SSID Interface.

nicid.description: The interface ID of the single Physical Interface, VLAN Interface, Modem Interface, ADSL Interface, or SSID Interface.

ne_ref.description: This represents a network element, which is a component that has an IP address and can be part of a network. It includes a location reference.

rank.description: The rank value to sort DNS entries, which must be a positive float. Only distinct values are accepted.

value.description: The IP address of the DNS server that the Firewall Cluster will use to resolve signature mirrors, domain names, and URL filtering categorization services (which are defined as URLs).

antispoofing_ne_ref.description: URI of the Network Element used for antispoofing.

path_count.description: The path count for equal cost multi-path routing, which determines the number of paths used for routing decisions.

bgp_as_ref.description: This represents the Autonomous System for Dynamic Routing Firewall functionality. The BGP Version is 4/4+. It includes the AS Number in decimal notation, which is used to identify the autonomous system in BGP routing.

bgp_profile_ref.description: This represents the BGP Profile for Dynamic Routing Firewall functionality, including port settings, distances, and BGP entries.

bmp_router_id.description: The BMP Router ID, which can be in the format [0-255]:[0-65535], V.X.Y.Z:[0-255], or [0-65535]:[0-255].

bmp_router_id_type.description: The BMP Router ID Type, which indicates the format of the BMP Router ID. Allowed values are 0 for [0-255]:[0-65535], 1 for V.X.Y.Z:[0-255], and 2 for [0-65535]:[0-255].

enabled.description: Indicates if BGP settings are enabled. If true, BGP routing is active.

router_id.description: The BGP Router ID, which can be an IPv4 address or null for automatic mode. Required for BGP configuration.

announced_ne_ref.description: This represents a network element, which is a component that has an IP address and can be part of a network. It includes a location reference.

announced_rm_ref.description: This represents a Route Map Policy for the Dynamic Routing Firewall settings, which is used to control the routing behavior based on specific rules.

block.description: This represents the BGP Dynamic Routing Firewall Settings, including BGP Profile, Router ID, and Autonomous System.

enabled.description: Indicates whether OSPFv2 Dynamic Routing is enabled.

ospfv2_profile_ref.description: This represents an abstract OSPF Profile used as Dynamic Routing element. It contains settings for OSPF routing, including distances and redistribution entries.

router_id.description: The OSPFv2 Router ID, which can be an IPv4 address or null for automatic mode.

block.description: This represents the OSPFv2 Dynamic Routing settings for the firewall, including whether it is enabled, the router ID, and the associated OSPFv2 profile.
This represents the Dynamic Routing Settings, which includes BGP and OSPFv2 settings, antispoofing networks, and path count for equal cost multi-path routing.

eca_client_config.description: This represents a ECA Client Configuration, which is used to manage the client-side configuration for ECA (Endpoint Compliance Agent). It includes settings such as trusted certificate authorities and auto-discovery options.

eca_client_network_ref.description: URI of the Network representing the client network for this ECA settings.

eca_server_network_ref.description: URI of the Network representing the server network for this ECA settings.

listened_zone_ref.description: URI of the Interface Zone representing the listened zone for this ECA settings.

listening_port.description: The port on which the ECA settings will listen for incoming connections.

address.description: The IP address associated with the single Physical Interface, VLAN Interface, Modem Interface, ADSL Interface, or SSID Interface.

nicid.description: The interface ID of the single Physical Interface, VLAN Interface, Modem Interface, ADSL Interface, or SSID Interface.

block.description: This represents the definition of ECA settings feature, which includes client and server networks, listened zones, listened interfaces, and listening port.

file_reputation_context.description: The file reputation context, which is required for the File Reputation Settings.

block.description: This represents the File Reputation settings for the Engine Cluster, including the file reputation context and HTTP proxies.

clat_local_ipv6_prefix_ip.description: The local IPv6 prefix address for 464XLAT CLAT mode, which is not required.

clat_local_ipv6_prefix_ref.description: This represents a Network, which is a Network Element that represents a (sub)network of computers. It includes attributes for IPv4 and IPv6 networks, broadcast address, and validation patterns.

clat_remote_ipv6_prefix_ip.description: The remote IPv6 prefix address for 464XLAT CLAT mode, which is not required.

clat_remote_ipv6_prefix_ref.description: This represents a Network, which is a Network Element that represents a (sub)network of computers. It includes attributes for IPv4 and IPv6 networks, broadcast address, and validation patterns.

mode.description: The mode for the IPv6 Transition Mechanism, which can be CLAT, NAT64, or SIIT EAM.

nat64_ipv6_prefix_ip.description: The IPv6 prefix address for NAT64 mode, which is not required.

nat64_ipv6_prefix_ref.description: This represents a Network, which is a Network Element that represents a (sub)network of computers. It includes attributes for IPv4 and IPv6 networks, broadcast address, and validation patterns.

nat64_local_pools_ref.description: URI of the Network representing the local IPv4 pools in NAT64 mode.

siit_eam_ipv6_pool_ip.description: The default IPv6 pool address for SIIT EAM mode, which is not required.

siit_eam_ipv6_pool_ref.description: This represents a Network, which is a Network Element that represents a (sub)network of computers. It includes attributes for IPv4 and IPv6 networks, broadcast address, and validation patterns.

comment.description: An optional comment for the NAT64 mapping.

nat64_mapping_protocol_ref.description: This represents an IP-proto service, which is used to define a service based on the IP protocol number. It includes a protocol number that specifies the protocol used by the traffic.

rank.description: The rank for ordering NAT64 mappings, where lower values indicate higher priority.

comment.description: An optional comment for the mapping.

snmp_location.description: The SNMP location for the engine node, which provides information about the physical location of the node.

cloud_id.description: The unique identifier for the appliance in the cloud service, such as an AWS instance ID.

pin_code.description: The PIN code used for the modem's SIM card. This is not required and can be used for modem configurations.

aggregate_mode.description: The aggregation type for the interface, which can be 'ha' for High Availability and represents two interfaces on the Firewall engine. Only the first interface in the aggregated link is actively used. The second interface becomes active only if the first interface fails. If you configure an Aggregated Link in High-Availability mode, connect the first interface to one switch and the second interface to another switch OR 'lb' for Load Balancing and Represents two interfaces on the Firewall engine. Both interfaces in the aggregated link are actively used and connections are automatically balanced between the two interfaces. Link aggregation in the load-balancing mode is implemented based on the IEEE 802.3ad Link Aggregation standard. If you configure an Aggregated Link in Load-Balancing Mode, connect both interfaces to a single switch. Make sure that the switch supports the Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP) and that LACP is configured on the switch.

atm_multiplexing_mode.description: The ATM Multiplexing Mode used for the ADSL connection.

comment.description: An optional comment for the element. This field is not required.

custom_configuration.description: Custom configuration for the physical interface, used for specific test or configuration purposes.

duplicate_address_detection.description: Indicates whether Duplicate Address Detection is enabled for IPv6, which helps prevent address conflicts on the network.

include_prefix_info_option_flag.description: Indicates whether the Include Prefix Information option is set in IPv6 Router Advertisements, which allows devices to automatically configure their IPv6 addresses based on the advertised prefixes.

interface_id.description: The Interface ID automatically maps to a physical network port of the same number during the initial configuration of the engine, but the mapping can be changed as necessary through the engine's command line interface. In case of VLAN Physical Interface, enter the VLAN ID (1-4094). The VLAN IDs you add must be the same as the VLAN IDs that are used in the switch at the other end of the VLAN trunk. Each VLAN Interface is identified as Interface-ID.VLAN-ID, for example 2.100 for Interface ID 2 and VLAN ID 100.

key.description: The unique identifier for the element. This field is required for updates but not for creation.

mac_prefix.description: The MAC Address prefix used for a shared interface, which is used to generate unique MAC addresses for interfaces in a shared configuration.

managed_address_flag.description: Indicates whether Managed Address Configuration is enabled in IPv6 Router Advertisements, which allows the Firewall to offer IPv6 addresses over DHCPv6.

mtu.description: The MTU (maximum transmission unit) size on the connected link. Either enter a value between 400-65535. The default value is 1500.

other_configuration_flag.description: Indicates whether Other Configuration is enabled in IPv6 Router Advertisements, which allows the Firewall to offer additional configuration information over DHCPv6.

override_engine_settings.description: Indicates whether the Engine's Default Settings are overridden for this interface, allowing for custom configurations.

override_log_moderation_settings.description: Indicates whether the Log Moderation settings are overridden for this interface, allowing for custom log moderation configurations.

qos_limit.description: The throughput limit for the link on this interface in kilobits per second (kbps). The same throughput is automatically applied to any VLANs created under this Physical Interface.

qos_mode.description: Defines how QoS is applied to the link on this interface, such as 'none', 'dscp_handling', 'full_qos', or 'throttling'.

qos_policy_ref.description: This represents a QoS Policy, which is used for Bandwidth Management and Traffic Prioritization based on QoS Classes or DSCP Matches.

router_advertisement.description: Indicates whether IPv6 Router Advertisements are sent, which provides configuration information to devices on the network.

second_interface_id.description: The second interface ID in the aggregated link, which is used in conjunction with the first interface for high availability or load balancing.

set_autonomous_address_flag.description: Indicates whether the Set Autonomous Address-Configuration option is set in IPv6 Router Advertisements, which allows devices to automatically configure their IPv6 addresses based on the advertised prefixes.

shared_interface.description: Indicates whether this interface is shared across multiple engines, allowing for shared configurations and resources.

syn_max_bursts.description: The SYN Burst Size value, which is the number of allowed SYNs before the engine starts limiting the SYN rate. Must be at least 1.

syn_mode.description: The SYN Rate Limits Mode, which can be 'off' for disabled, 'auto' for automatic calculation, or 'custom' for manual settings.

syn_per_second.description: The Allowed SYNs per Second value, which is the number of allowed SYN packets per second. Must be at least 1.

vci.description: The Virtual Channel Identifier (VCI) used in the ADSL connection.

vpi.description: The Virtual Path Identifier (VPI) used in the ADSL connection.

zone_ref.description: This represents a Zone, which is used to group together network interfaces of Firewall, IPS, and Layer 2 Firewall engines. Zones can be used to specify receiving or sending interfaces in policies and automatically apply to new interfaces associated with the same Zone.

ipaddress.description: The IP address associated with the ARP entry, which can be either IPv4 or IPv6.

macaddress.description: The MAC address associated with the ARP entry. It is not required but can be provided for static entries.

netmask.description: The netmask for the ARP entry, which defines the network portion of the IP address. It can be a value between 0 and 128 for IPv6.

type.description: The type of ARP entry, which can be 'static' for permanent references or 'dynamic' for proxy ARP. 'static': it gives the engine a permanent reference to an IP address/MAC address pair. All entries are of this type on IPS engines, Layer 2 Firewalls, Master Engines, and Virtual NGFW Engines. 'dynamic': it gives a Firewall engine a reference to an IP address/MAC address pair that the Firewall should perform proxy ARP for. Proxy ARP is possible only for hosts located in networks directly connected to the Firewall.

max_packet_size.description: The maximum packet size for DHCP Relay, which is required if DHCP Relay is enabled.

trusted_circuit.description: Indicates whether the DHCP Relay is configured for a trusted circuit.

default_gateway.description: The IP address of the Default Gateway through which traffic from clients is routed.

default_lease_time.description: The Default Lease Time in seconds after which IP addresses assigned to clients must be renewed.

dhcp_address_range.description: The manual DHCP address range or address in the same network space defined for the Physical Interface.

dhcp_range_ref.description: This represents an Address Range, which is a Network Element that defines a range of IP addresses. It includes attributes for the range of IP addresses, which must be valid IPv4 or IPv6 addresses.

domain_name_search_list.description: The 'search list' of Domain Names to be used by the client to locate not-fully-qualified domain names.

primary_dns_server.description: The Primary DNS Server IP address that clients use to resolve domain names.

primary_wins_server.description: The Primary WINS Server IP address that clients use to resolve NetBIOS computer names.

secondary_dns_server.description: The Secondary DNS Server IP address that clients use to resolve domain names.

secondary_wins_server.description: The Secondary WINS Server IP address that clients use to resolve NetBIOS computer names.

node_id.description: The ID of the DHCP node. This ID is used to identify the node in the cluster.

max_packet_size.description: The maximum packet size for DHCP Relay, which is required if DHCP Relay is enabled.

trusted_circuit.description: Indicates whether the DHCP Relay is configured for a trusted circuit.

burst.description: The maximum number of matching log entries in a single burst. The default value for Antispoofing entries is 1000. By default, Discard log entries are not compressed.

log_event.description: The type of log event for moderation.

rate.description: The maximum number of log entries per second.

qos_limit.description: The QoS interface throughput limit for the Virtual Resource, specified in kbps.

virtual_mapping.description: The identifier for the Virtual Mapping associated with this Virtual Resource.

virtual_resource_name.description: The name of the Virtual Resource associated with these settings.

block.description: This represents an ADSL physical interface, which is used for connecting to ADSL networks. It supports various ADSL standards and is applicable only to specific appliances with integrated ADSL network interface cards.

aggregate_mode.description: The aggregation type for the interface, which can be 'ha' for High Availability and represents two interfaces on the Firewall engine. Only the first interface in the aggregated link is actively used. The second interface becomes active only if the first interface fails. If you configure an Aggregated Link in High-Availability mode, connect the first interface to one switch and the second interface to another switch OR 'lb' for Load Balancing and Represents two interfaces on the Firewall engine. Both interfaces in the aggregated link are actively used and connections are automatically balanced between the two interfaces. Link aggregation in the load-balancing mode is implemented based on the IEEE 802.3ad Link Aggregation standard. If you configure an Aggregated Link in Load-Balancing Mode, connect both interfaces to a single switch. Make sure that the switch supports the Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP) and that LACP is configured on the switch.

comment.description: An optional comment for the element. This field is not required.

custom_configuration.description: Custom configuration for the physical interface, used for specific test or configuration purposes.

duplicate_address_detection.description: Indicates whether Duplicate Address Detection is enabled for IPv6, which helps prevent address conflicts on the network.

include_prefix_info_option_flag.description: Indicates whether the Include Prefix Information option is set in IPv6 Router Advertisements, which allows devices to automatically configure their IPv6 addresses based on the advertised prefixes.

interface_id.description: The Interface ID automatically maps to a physical network port of the same number during the initial configuration of the engine, but the mapping can be changed as necessary through the engine's command line interface. In case of VLAN Physical Interface, enter the VLAN ID (1-4094). The VLAN IDs you add must be the same as the VLAN IDs that are used in the switch at the other end of the VLAN trunk. Each VLAN Interface is identified as Interface-ID.VLAN-ID, for example 2.100 for Interface ID 2 and VLAN ID 100.

key.description: The unique identifier for the element. This field is required for updates but not for creation.

mac_prefix.description: The MAC Address prefix used for a shared interface, which is used to generate unique MAC addresses for interfaces in a shared configuration.

managed_address_flag.description: Indicates whether Managed Address Configuration is enabled in IPv6 Router Advertisements, which allows the Firewall to offer IPv6 addresses over DHCPv6.

modem_auth_method.description: The authentication method used for the Modem Interface, applicable for 4G/LTE modems.

modem_interface_type.description: The type of the Modem Interface, indicating whether it is a 3G or 4G/LTE modem.

mtu.description: The MTU (maximum transmission unit) size on the connected link. Either enter a value between 400-65535. The default value is 1500.

other_configuration_flag.description: Indicates whether Other Configuration is enabled in IPv6 Router Advertisements, which allows the Firewall to offer additional configuration information over DHCPv6.

override_engine_settings.description: Indicates whether the Engine's Default Settings are overridden for this interface, allowing for custom configurations.

override_log_moderation_settings.description: Indicates whether the Log Moderation settings are overridden for this interface, allowing for custom log moderation configurations.

qos_limit.description: The throughput limit for the link on this interface in kilobits per second (kbps). The same throughput is automatically applied to any VLANs created under this Physical Interface.

qos_mode.description: Defines how QoS is applied to the link on this interface, such as 'none', 'dscp_handling', 'full_qos', or 'throttling'.

qos_policy_ref.description: This represents a QoS Policy, which is used for Bandwidth Management and Traffic Prioritization based on QoS Classes or DSCP Matches.

router_advertisement.description: Indicates whether IPv6 Router Advertisements are sent, which provides configuration information to devices on the network.

second_interface_id.description: The second interface ID in the aggregated link, which is used in conjunction with the first interface for high availability or load balancing.

set_autonomous_address_flag.description: Indicates whether the Set Autonomous Address-Configuration option is set in IPv6 Router Advertisements, which allows devices to automatically configure their IPv6 addresses based on the advertised prefixes.

shared_interface.description: Indicates whether this interface is shared across multiple engines, allowing for shared configurations and resources.

syn_max_bursts.description: The SYN Burst Size value, which is the number of allowed SYNs before the engine starts limiting the SYN rate. Must be at least 1.

syn_mode.description: The SYN Rate Limits Mode, which can be 'off' for disabled, 'auto' for automatic calculation, or 'custom' for manual settings.

syn_per_second.description: The Allowed SYNs per Second value, which is the number of allowed SYN packets per second. Must be at least 1.

zone_ref.description: This represents a Zone, which is used to group together network interfaces of Firewall, IPS, and Layer 2 Firewall engines. Zones can be used to specify receiving or sending interfaces in policies and automatically apply to new interfaces associated with the same Zone.

ipaddress.description: The IP address associated with the ARP entry, which can be either IPv4 or IPv6.

macaddress.description: The MAC address associated with the ARP entry. It is not required but can be provided for static entries.

netmask.description: The netmask for the ARP entry, which defines the network portion of the IP address. It can be a value between 0 and 128 for IPv6.

type.description: The type of ARP entry, which can be 'static' for permanent references or 'dynamic' for proxy ARP. 'static': it gives the engine a permanent reference to an IP address/MAC address pair. All entries are of this type on IPS engines, Layer 2 Firewalls, Master Engines, and Virtual NGFW Engines. 'dynamic': it gives a Firewall engine a reference to an IP address/MAC address pair that the Firewall should perform proxy ARP for. Proxy ARP is possible only for hosts located in networks directly connected to the Firewall.

enabled.description: Indicates whether the DHCP Relay is enabled on this interface.

max_packet_size.description: The maximum packet size for DHCP Relay, which is required if DHCP Relay is enabled.

trusted_circuit.description: Indicates whether the DHCP Relay is configured for a trusted circuit.

block.description: This represents the definition of DHCP Relay on an interface, allowing you to select which firewall interfaces perform DHCP relay and activate it towards the DHCP clients.

default_gateway.description: The IP address of the Default Gateway through which traffic from clients is routed.

default_lease_time.description: The Default Lease Time in seconds after which IP addresses assigned to clients must be renewed.

dhcp_address_range.description: The manual DHCP address range or address in the same network space defined for the Physical Interface.

dhcp_range_ref.description: This represents an Address Range, which is a Network Element that defines a range of IP addresses. It includes attributes for the range of IP addresses, which must be valid IPv4 or IPv6 addresses.

domain_name_search_list.description: The 'search list' of Domain Names to be used by the client to locate not-fully-qualified domain names.

primary_dns_server.description: The Primary DNS Server IP address that clients use to resolve domain names.

primary_wins_server.description: The Primary WINS Server IP address that clients use to resolve NetBIOS computer names.

secondary_dns_server.description: The Secondary DNS Server IP address that clients use to resolve domain names.

secondary_wins_server.description: The Secondary WINS Server IP address that clients use to resolve NetBIOS computer names.

burst.description: The maximum number of matching log entries in a single burst. The default value for Antispoofing entries is 1000. By default, Discard log entries are not compressed.

log_event.description: The type of log event for moderation.

rate.description: The maximum number of log entries per second.

qos_limit.description: The QoS interface throughput limit for the Virtual Resource, specified in kbps.

virtual_mapping.description: The identifier for the Virtual Mapping associated with this Virtual Resource.

virtual_resource_name.description: The name of the Virtual Resource associated with these settings.

block.description: This represents a Modem Interface, which is used for defining the settings of a 3G or 4G/LTE modem. It includes attributes for modem type and authentication method.

aggregate_mode.description: The aggregation type for the interface, which can be 'ha' for High Availability and represents two interfaces on the Firewall engine. Only the first interface in the aggregated link is actively used. The second interface becomes active only if the first interface fails. If you configure an Aggregated Link in High-Availability mode, connect the first interface to one switch and the second interface to another switch OR 'lb' for Load Balancing and Represents two interfaces on the Firewall engine. Both interfaces in the aggregated link are actively used and connections are automatically balanced between the two interfaces. Link aggregation in the load-balancing mode is implemented based on the IEEE 802.3ad Link Aggregation standard. If you configure an Aggregated Link in Load-Balancing Mode, connect both interfaces to a single switch. Make sure that the switch supports the Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP) and that LACP is configured on the switch.

comment.description: An optional comment for the element. This field is not required.

custom_configuration.description: Custom configuration for the physical interface, used for specific test or configuration purposes.

cvi_mode.description: The Cluster Virtual IP Address (CVI) mode for the physical interface. The Packet Dispatch (packetdispatch) mode is the best choice in most environments.

duplicate_address_detection.description: Indicates whether Duplicate Address Detection is enabled for IPv6, which helps prevent address conflicts on the network.

include_prefix_info_option_flag.description: Indicates whether the Include Prefix Information option is set in IPv6 Router Advertisements, which allows devices to automatically configure their IPv6 addresses based on the advertised prefixes.

interface_id.description: The Interface ID automatically maps to a physical network port of the same number during the initial configuration of the engine, but the mapping can be changed as necessary through the engine's command line interface. In case of VLAN Physical Interface, enter the VLAN ID (1-4094). The VLAN IDs you add must be the same as the VLAN IDs that are used in the switch at the other end of the VLAN trunk. Each VLAN Interface is identified as Interface-ID.VLAN-ID, for example 2.100 for Interface ID 2 and VLAN ID 100.

key.description: The unique identifier for the element. This field is required for updates but not for creation.

lldp_mode.description: The LLDP (Link Layer Discovery Protocol) mode for the physical interface.

mac_prefix.description: The MAC Address prefix used for a shared interface, which is used to generate unique MAC addresses for interfaces in a shared configuration.

macaddress.description: The MAC address for the Cluster Virtual IP Address. Use a unicast MAC address for packetdispatch and unicast modes, or a multicast MAC address for multicast mode.

managed_address_flag.description: Indicates whether Managed Address Configuration is enabled in IPv6 Router Advertisements, which allows the Firewall to offer IPv6 addresses over DHCPv6.

mtu.description: The MTU (maximum transmission unit) size on the connected link. Either enter a value between 400-65535. The default value is 1500.

multicast_ip.description: The multicast IP address used for automatically calculating a MAC address in multicastigmp mode. IP address from the range 224.0.0.0-239.255.255.255.

other_configuration_flag.description: Indicates whether Other Configuration is enabled in IPv6 Router Advertisements, which allows the Firewall to offer additional configuration information over DHCPv6.

override_engine_settings.description: Indicates whether the Engine's Default Settings are overridden for this interface, allowing for custom configurations.

override_log_moderation_settings.description: Indicates whether the Log Moderation settings are overridden for this interface, allowing for custom log moderation configurations.

qos_limit.description: The throughput limit for the link on this interface in kilobits per second (kbps). The same throughput is automatically applied to any VLANs created under this Physical Interface.

qos_mode.description: Defines how QoS is applied to the link on this interface, such as 'none', 'dscp_handling', 'full_qos', or 'throttling'.

qos_policy_ref.description: This represents a QoS Policy, which is used for Bandwidth Management and Traffic Prioritization based on QoS Classes or DSCP Matches.

route_replies_back_ipv4_address.description: The IPv4 address for the Route Replies Back. If Route Replies Back Mode is enabled, either a Route Replies Back IPv4 or IPv6 Address is required.

route_replies_back_ipv6_address.description: The IPv6 address for the Route Replies Back. If Route Replies Back Mode is enabled, either a Route Replies Back IPv4 or IPv6 Address is required.

route_replies_back_mode.description: Indicates whether the Route Replies Back Mode is enabled. If enabled, either a Route Replies Back IPv4 or IPv6 Address is required.

router_advertisement.description: Indicates whether IPv6 Router Advertisements are sent, which provides configuration information to devices on the network.

second_interface_id.description: The second interface ID in the aggregated link, which is used in conjunction with the first interface for high availability or load balancing.

set_autonomous_address_flag.description: Indicates whether the Set Autonomous Address-Configuration option is set in IPv6 Router Advertisements, which allows devices to automatically configure their IPv6 addresses based on the advertised prefixes.

shared_interface.description: Indicates whether this interface is shared across multiple engines, allowing for shared configurations and resources.

syn_max_bursts.description: The SYN Burst Size value, which is the number of allowed SYNs before the engine starts limiting the SYN rate. Must be at least 1.

syn_mode.description: The SYN Rate Limits Mode, which can be 'off' for disabled, 'auto' for automatic calculation, or 'custom' for manual settings.

syn_per_second.description: The Allowed SYNs per Second value, which is the number of allowed SYN packets per second. Must be at least 1.

virtual_engine_vlan_ok.description: Indicates whether VLANs can be created under this interface in a virtual engine. This is applicable for interfaces of a master node in a cluster.

zone_ref.description: This represents a Zone, which is used to group together network interfaces of Firewall, IPS, and Layer 2 Firewall engines. Zones can be used to specify receiving or sending interfaces in policies and automatically apply to new interfaces associated with the same Zone.

ipaddress.description: The IP address associated with the ARP entry, which can be either IPv4 or IPv6.

macaddress.description: The MAC address associated with the ARP entry. It is not required but can be provided for static entries.

netmask.description: The netmask for the ARP entry, which defines the network portion of the IP address. It can be a value between 0 and 128 for IPv6.

type.description: The type of ARP entry, which can be 'static' for permanent references or 'dynamic' for proxy ARP. 'static': it gives the engine a permanent reference to an IP address/MAC address pair. All entries are of this type on IPS engines, Layer 2 Firewalls, Master Engines, and Virtual NGFW Engines. 'dynamic': it gives a Firewall engine a reference to an IP address/MAC address pair that the Firewall should perform proxy ARP for. Proxy ARP is possible only for hosts located in networks directly connected to the Firewall.

burst.description: The maximum number of matching log entries in a single burst. The default value for Antispoofing entries is 1000. By default, Discard log entries are not compressed.

log_event.description: The type of log event for moderation.

rate.description: The maximum number of log entries per second.

full_sync_interval.description: The Full Synchronization Interface value (in milliseconds), which defines how frequently the full synchronizations are done. Do not set the values much higher or lower than their defaults (5000 ms for full). Caution! Adjusting the Sync Intervals has significant impact on the cluster's performance. Inappropriate settings seriously degrade the firewall's performance.

heartbeat_group_ip.description: A valid Heartbeat Synchronization Group IP Address (IPv4 or IPv6) between '224.0.0.0 and 239.255.255.255' if you want to change the multicast IP addresses used for node-to-node communications (default: 225.1.1.1). This multicast IP address must not be used for other purposes on any of the network interfaces.

incr_sync_interval.description: The Incremental Synchronization Interface value (in milliseconds), which defines how frequently the incremental synchronizations are done. Do not set the values much higher or lower than their defaults (50 ms for incremental). Caution! Adjusting the Sync Intervals has significant impact on the cluster's performance. Inappropriate settings seriously degrade the firewall's performance.

statesync_group_ip.description: A valid State Synchronization Group IP Address (IPv4 or IPv6) between '224.0.0.0 and 239.255.255.255' if you want to change the multicast IP addresses used for node-to-node communications (default: 225.1.1.2). This multicast IP address must not be used for other purposes on any of the network interfaces.

sync_mode.description: The synchronization mode for the cluster, which defines how nodes exchange information about the traffic they process. 'sync_all': (recommended) both full and incremental synchronization messages are sent. This allows frequent updates without consuming resources excessively. Regular full synchronization ensures that all nodes stay synchronized even if some incremental messages are not delivered. 'sync_full': (not recommended) Only full synchronization messages are sent. Incremental updates are not sent in between, so nodes may not have the same information on connections unless the full sync interval is significantly reduced.

sync_security.description: The Synchronization Security Level, which defines the security features for synchronization. 'none': no security features. Do not select this option unless the heartbeat traffic uses a dedicated, secure network that does not handle other traffic. 'sign': (default) transmissions are authenticated to prevent outside injections of connection state information. 'encrypt': transmissions are authenticated and encrypted. This option increases the overhead compared to the default option, but is strongly recommended if the node-to-node communications are relayed through insecure networks (for example, if the backup heartbeat is configured on an interface that handles other traffic).

block.description: This represents the synchronization parameters for a cluster of engines, including sync mode, intervals, security level, and multicast IP addresses.

qos_limit.description: The QoS interface throughput limit for the Virtual Resource, specified in kbps.

virtual_mapping.description: The identifier for the Virtual Mapping associated with this Virtual Resource.

virtual_resource_name.description: The name of the Virtual Resource associated with these settings.

aggregate_mode.description: The aggregation type for the interface, which can be 'ha' for High Availability and represents two interfaces on the Firewall engine. Only the first interface in the aggregated link is actively used. The second interface becomes active only if the first interface fails. If you configure an Aggregated Link in High-Availability mode, connect the first interface to one switch and the second interface to another switch OR 'lb' for Load Balancing and Represents two interfaces on the Firewall engine. Both interfaces in the aggregated link are actively used and connections are automatically balanced between the two interfaces. Link aggregation in the load-balancing mode is implemented based on the IEEE 802.3ad Link Aggregation standard. If you configure an Aggregated Link in Load-Balancing Mode, connect both interfaces to a single switch. Make sure that the switch supports the Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP) and that LACP is configured on the switch.

custom_configuration.description: Custom configuration for the physical interface, used for specific test or configuration purposes.

duplicate_address_detection.description: Indicates whether Duplicate Address Detection is enabled for IPv6, which helps prevent address conflicts on the network.

include_prefix_info_option_flag.description: Indicates whether the Include Prefix Information option is set in IPv6 Router Advertisements, which allows devices to automatically configure their IPv6 addresses based on the advertised prefixes.

interface_id.description: The Interface ID automatically maps to a physical network port of the same number during the initial configuration of the engine, but the mapping can be changed as necessary through the engine's command line interface. In case of VLAN Physical Interface, enter the VLAN ID (1-4094). The VLAN IDs you add must be the same as the VLAN IDs that are used in the switch at the other end of the VLAN trunk. Each VLAN Interface is identified as Interface-ID.VLAN-ID, for example 2.100 for Interface ID 2 and VLAN ID 100.

key.description: The unique identifier for the element. This field is required for updates but not for creation.

mac_prefix.description: The MAC Address prefix used for a shared interface, which is used to generate unique MAC addresses for interfaces in a shared configuration.

managed_address_flag.description: Indicates whether Managed Address Configuration is enabled in IPv6 Router Advertisements, which allows the Firewall to offer IPv6 addresses over DHCPv6.

mtu.description: The MTU (maximum transmission unit) size on the connected link. Either enter a value between 400-65535. The default value is 1500.

other_configuration_flag.description: Indicates whether Other Configuration is enabled in IPv6 Router Advertisements, which allows the Firewall to offer additional configuration information over DHCPv6.

override_engine_settings.description: Indicates whether the Engine's Default Settings are overridden for this interface, allowing for custom configurations.

override_log_moderation_settings.description: Indicates whether the Log Moderation settings are overridden for this interface, allowing for custom log moderation configurations.

qos_limit.description: The throughput limit for the link on this interface in kilobits per second (kbps). The same throughput is automatically applied to any VLANs created under this Physical Interface.

qos_mode.description: Defines how QoS is applied to the link on this interface, such as 'none', 'dscp_handling', 'full_qos', or 'throttling'.

qos_policy_ref.description: This represents a QoS Policy, which is used for Bandwidth Management and Traffic Prioritization based on QoS Classes or DSCP Matches.

route_replies_back_ipv4_address.description: An IPv4 address for the Route Replies Back. If Route Replies Back Mode is enabled, either a Route Replies Back IPv4 or IPv6 Address is required.

route_replies_back_ipv6_address.description: An IPv6 address for the Route Replies Back. If Route Replies Back Mode is enabled, either a Route Replies Back IPv4 or IPv6 Address is required.

route_replies_back_mode.description: Indicates whether the Route Replies Back Mode is enabled for this interface.

router_advertisement.description: Indicates whether IPv6 Router Advertisements are sent, which provides configuration information to devices on the network.

second_interface_id.description: The second interface ID in the aggregated link, which is used in conjunction with the first interface for high availability or load balancing.

set_autonomous_address_flag.description: Indicates whether the Set Autonomous Address-Configuration option is set in IPv6 Router Advertisements, which allows devices to automatically configure their IPv6 addresses based on the advertised prefixes.

shared_interface.description: Indicates whether this interface is shared across multiple engines, allowing for shared configurations and resources.

syn_max_bursts.description: The SYN Burst Size value, which is the number of allowed SYNs before the engine starts limiting the SYN rate. Must be at least 1.

syn_mode.description: The SYN Rate Limits Mode, which can be 'off' for disabled, 'auto' for automatic calculation, or 'custom' for manual settings.

syn_per_second.description: The Allowed SYNs per Second value, which is the number of allowed SYN packets per second. Must be at least 1.

zone_ref.description: This represents a Zone, which is used to group together network interfaces of Firewall, IPS, and Layer 2 Firewall engines. Zones can be used to specify receiving or sending interfaces in policies and automatically apply to new interfaces associated with the same Zone.

ipaddress.description: The IP address associated with the ARP entry, which can be either IPv4 or IPv6.

macaddress.description: The MAC address associated with the ARP entry. It is not required but can be provided for static entries.

netmask.description: The netmask for the ARP entry, which defines the network portion of the IP address. It can be a value between 0 and 128 for IPv6.

type.description: The type of ARP entry, which can be 'static' for permanent references or 'dynamic' for proxy ARP. 'static': it gives the engine a permanent reference to an IP address/MAC address pair. All entries are of this type on IPS engines, Layer 2 Firewalls, Master Engines, and Virtual NGFW Engines. 'dynamic': it gives a Firewall engine a reference to an IP address/MAC address pair that the Firewall should perform proxy ARP for. Proxy ARP is possible only for hosts located in networks directly connected to the Firewall.

enabled.description: Indicates whether the DHCP Relay is enabled on this interface.

max_packet_size.description: The maximum packet size for DHCP Relay, which is required if DHCP Relay is enabled.

trusted_circuit.description: Indicates whether the DHCP Relay is configured for a trusted circuit.

block.description: This represents the definition of DHCP Relay on an interface, allowing you to select which firewall interfaces perform DHCP relay and activate it towards the DHCP clients.

default_gateway.description: The IP address of the Default Gateway through which traffic from clients is routed.

default_lease_time.description: The Default Lease Time in seconds after which IP addresses assigned to clients must be renewed.

dhcp_address_range.description: The manual DHCP address range or address in the same network space defined for the Physical Interface.

dhcp_range_ref.description: This represents an Address Range, which is a Network Element that defines a range of IP addresses. It includes attributes for the range of IP addresses, which must be valid IPv4 or IPv6 addresses.

domain_name_search_list.description: The 'search list' of Domain Names to be used by the client to locate not-fully-qualified domain names.

primary_dns_server.description: The Primary DNS Server IP address that clients use to resolve domain names.

primary_wins_server.description: The Primary WINS Server IP address that clients use to resolve NetBIOS computer names.

secondary_dns_server.description: The Secondary DNS Server IP address that clients use to resolve domain names.

secondary_wins_server.description: The Secondary WINS Server IP address that clients use to resolve NetBIOS computer names.

dhcp_address_range.description: The IPv4 address range for the DHCP server, specified in the format X.X.X.X-Y.Y.Y.Y or as a single IPv4 address X.X.X.X.

node_id.description: The ID of the DHCP node. This ID is used to identify the node in the cluster.

block.description: This represents the definition of DHCP Server on an interface, which includes settings for IP ranges, DNS servers, WINS servers, gateways, and lease times.

enabled.description: Indicates whether the DHCP Relay is enabled on this interface.

max_packet_size.description: The maximum packet size for DHCP Relay, which is required if DHCP Relay is enabled.

trusted_circuit.description: Indicates whether the DHCP Relay is configured for a trusted circuit.

block.description: This represents the definition of DHCP Relay on an interface, allowing you to select which firewall interfaces perform DHCP relay and activate it towards the DHCP clients.

address.description: The IP Address (IPv4 or IPv6) of the interface. For dynamic interfaces, this will be null.

comment.description: An optional comment for the element. This field is not required.

inspect_qinq.description: Indicates whether QinQ is inspected or not. This option allows the IPS engine to inspect traffic that uses QinQ encapsulation.

inspect_unspecified_vlans.description: Indicates whether unspecified VLANs are inspected or not. Deselect this option to make the IPS engine ignore traffic from VLANs that are not included in the IPS engine's interface configuration. We recommend that you keep this option selected if you do not have a specific reason to deselect it.

logical_interface_ref.description: This represents a Logical Interface. It is an IPS Element used in the IPS policies to represent one or more physical network interfaces as defined in the IPS engine properties.

network_value.description: The IP Network (IPv4 or IPv6) of the interface. For dynamic interfaces, this will be null.

nicid.description: The Interface ID of the interface.

reset_interface_nicid.description: The Reset Interface to specify the interface through which TCP connection resets are sent when Reset responses are used in your IPS policy.

block.description: This represents an IPS Engine interface that can listen to traffic passing in the network, but which is not used for routing traffic through the engine.

address.description: The IP Address (IPv4 or IPv6) of the interface. For dynamic interfaces, this will be null.

comment.description: An optional comment for the element. This field is not required.

igmp_mode.description: The IGMP mode for this interface, which can be 'upstream' or 'downstream'. In upstream mode, the firewall acts as an IGMP querier for multicast servers and hosts in local networks. In downstream mode, the firewall queries downstream networks for hosts that want to join or leave multicast host groups.

igmp_version.description: The IGMP version used by this interface, which can be 1, 2, or 3. The default version is 3, but you may need to select another version for compatibility with certain hosts.

nicid.description: The Interface ID of the interface.

relayed_by_dhcp.description: Indicates whether this interface is relayed by DHCP. This option is used to specify if the interface is relayed by DHCP, which can be useful in certain network configurations.

pin_code.description: The PIN code used for the modem's SIM card. This is not required and can be used for modem configurations.

pppoe.description: Indicates whether this interface is configured for PPPoE (Point-to-Point Protocol over Ethernet).

pppoe_password.description: The PPPoE password used for authentication when the interface is configured for PPPoE.

pppoe_servicename.description: The PPPoE service name used for the interface when configured for PPPoE.

pppoe_username.description: The PPPoE username used for authentication when the interface is configured for PPPoE.

primary_heartbeat.description: Indicates whether this interface is the primary heartbeat interface for communications between the nodes. There must be one and only one primary heartbeat interface.

primary_mgt.description: Indicates whether this interface is the primary control interface for management server contact. There must be one and only one primary control interface.

reverse_connection.description: Indicates whether reverse connection is enabled for this interface. This is not required and can be used to allow reverse connections.

vrrp_priority.description: The VRRP priority used for the interface when configured for VRRP. This is required only for VRRP mode and must be a valid integer.

heartbeat_group_ip.description: A valid Heartbeat Synchronization Group IP Address (IPv4 or IPv6) between '224.0.0.0 and 239.255.255.255' if you want to change the multicast IP addresses used for node-to-node communications (default: 225.1.1.1). This multicast IP address must not be used for other purposes on any of the network interfaces.

incr_sync_interval.description: The Incremental Synchronization Interface value (in milliseconds), which defines how frequently the incremental synchronizations are done. Do not set the values much higher or lower than their defaults (50 ms for incremental). Caution! Adjusting the Sync Intervals has significant impact on the cluster's performance. Inappropriate settings seriously degrade the firewall's performance.

statesync_group_ip.description: A valid State Synchronization Group IP Address (IPv4 or IPv6) between '224.0.0.0 and 239.255.255.255' if you want to change the multicast IP addresses used for node-to-node communications (default: 225.1.1.2). This multicast IP address must not be used for other purposes on any of the network interfaces.

sync_mode.description: The synchronization mode for the cluster, which defines how nodes exchange information about the traffic they process. 'sync_all': (recommended) both full and incremental synchronization messages are sent. This allows frequent updates without consuming resources excessively. Regular full synchronization ensures that all nodes stay synchronized even if some incremental messages are not delivered. 'sync_full': (not recommended) Only full synchronization messages are sent. Incremental updates are not sent in between, so nodes may not have the same information on connections unless the full sync interval is significantly reduced.

sync_security.description: The Synchronization Security Level, which defines the security features for synchronization. 'none': no security features. Do not select this option unless the heartbeat traffic uses a dedicated, secure network that does not handle other traffic. 'sign': (default) transmissions are authenticated to prevent outside injections of connection state information. 'encrypt': transmissions are authenticated and encrypted. This option increases the overhead compared to the default option, but is strongly recommended if the node-to-node communications are relayed through insecure networks (for example, if the backup heartbeat is configured on an interface that handles other traffic).
