system_key.description: The system key of the System element. This field is not required.

trashed.description: Indicates if the element is trashed. This field is not required.

trust_all_cas.description: Indicates whether to trust all certificate authorities (CAs) or not. If set to true, all CAs are trusted without validation.

trusted_certificate_authority.description: URI of the VPN Certificate Authority.

tunnel_life_time_kbytes.description: IPsec Lifetime in KBytes. This is the maximum amount of data that can be sent before the IPsec SA is rekeyed.

sha2_ike_hash_length.description: The SHA2 hash length used for IKE (Internet Key Exchange).

sha2_ipsec_hash_length.description: The SHA2 hash length used for IPsec (Internet Protocol Security).

block.description: This represents the capabilities of a gateway or VPN profile, including various cryptographic and protocol features.
This represents a VPN Profile. It contains settings for IKE and IPsec lifetimes, keep-alive options, certificate authorities, and authentication methods.

admin_domain.description: This represents a Domain. Domains are administrative boundaries that allow you to separate the configuration details and other information in the system for the purpose of limiting administrator access.

automatic.description: Indicates whether this site is automatically created or manually added. If true, the site is automatically created and cannot have VPN references set.

comment.description: An optional comment for the element. This field is not required.

etag.description: The ETag of the element, used for versioning. This field is not required.

gateway.description: This represents a VPN Gateway. A VPN Gateway is a network element that can be used to establish a VPN connection with other gateways.

id.description: this attribute is the identifier of terraform resource

key.description: The unique identifier for the element. This field is required for updates but not for creation.

locked.description: Indicates if the element is locked. This field is not required.

read_only.description: Indicates if the element is read-only. This field is not required.

system.description: Indicates if the element is a System element. This field is not required.

system_key.description: The system key of the System element. This field is not required.

trashed.description: Indicates if the element is trashed. This field is not required.

block.description: This represents a VPN Site, which is a collection of network elements that are part of a VPN. It can be associated with a gateway and has references to VPNs.

href.description: The API href of the element.

type.description: The type of the element.

elements.description: List of elements matching the search criteria.

href.description: returns the href of the first available element

id.description: Data source identifier.

name.description: The name pattern to search for. Supports wildcard matching using '*' (e.g., 'All Router*').

type.description: The type of SMC element to search for (e.g., 'host', 'network', 'group').

block.description: Element data source allows searching for multiple SMC elements by type and name pattern. Supports wildcard matching using '*' in the name.

from_ref.description:
The url from where to search for sub-element.

e.g. to start searching for the href of an internal gateway or its
sub-elements of a given firewall, use:

	from_ref = "http://mysmc:8082/7.4/elements/single_fw/268587556/internal_gateway"

Note that you should not have raw urls like this in your terraform
file: The url of a resource such as a single firewall is accessible
via the terraform "id" attribute or via its "lk" attribute, example:

    from_ref = "${smc_single_fw.my_single_fw.id}/internal_gateway"

could also be written:

    from_ref = smc_single_fw.my_single_fw.lk.internal_gateway

id.description: returns the href of the sub-resource matching query

match.description:
An expression to locate the desired sub-element.
e.g. to get and endpoint from firewall reference, you need a match expression like this:

	match="mygateway/internal_endpoint/192.168.100.14"

block.description:
Enables the retrieval of the "href" (aka "id" or "url") of a nested resources.

For example, it can be used to obtain the "href" of sub-resources that
are implicitly created along with a firewall, such as internal
gateways or endpoints.

	data "smc_sub_href" "ep_192_168_100_14" {
		from_ref = "http://mysmc:8082/7.4/elements/single_fw/268587556/internal_gateway"
		match = "mygateway/internal_endpoint/192.168.100.14"
	}

then you would use it this way:

	locals {
       # the value of my_endpoint_id would be something like:
       # http://localhost:8082/7.4/elements/single_fw/12345/internal_gateway/6789/internal_endpoint/101112
	   my_endpoint_id = data.smc_sub_href.ep_192_168_100_14.id
	}
